properties.name: A served skill carries a line a person reads and says who it is for, beside the trigger an agent matches on — so no consumer writes its own summaries
properties.statement: Anthony, 2026-09-19 ('start addressing the issues identified in flo2 and bhome feedback docs'), promoting flo2 F8/F9. The served surface stated what a person TYPES (the shortcut, gate-compared since cap:the-command-surface-answers-for-itself) and nothing a person READS: all 30 descriptions open 'Use …' (250–878 chars, median 437) because their job is the agent's trigger, so a consumer building a menu stripped the opener by hand or kept 30 summaries a rename would make quietly wrong. Every skill must carry `summary` (one line addressed to a person, never trigger-shaped, at most 120 characters) and `audience` (anyone / operator / agent — expertise, not human-versus-model), required at build and by the lint, served by list_skills and get_skill. Any count the surface states about itself is computed, never written ('eight of these differ' was nine, then ten).
